newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian state mediator averts major strike.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian state mediator averts major strike.

text.p: Norway early on Monday averted a crippling strike by 250,000 workers when labour and management negotiators accepted a mediated solution on early retirement and wage increases, media reports said.
A threatened walkout on Monday by about 12 percent of Norway's labour force would have halted ferries, many domestic flights and most of the construction industry.
The strike could have eventually curbed oil production because it would have hit supplies and transport to and from platforms.
Norway, which pumps more than three million barrels of oil per day, is the world's second largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia.

The reports said the Confederation of Trade Unions (LO) and the employers' Confederation of Trade and Industry (NHO) agreed to proposals by government-appointed chief mediator Reidar Webster on outstanding differences.
"This is the best pension agreement we could have received," LO Chairman Yngve Haagensen told Norwegian television.
NHO leader Karl Glad told the national news agency NTB: "We had to give in on early retirement in order to save the peace on the labour market."
LO broke off talks with NHO last month because the latter refused to accept early retirement at 62 and 63 years of age for some workers. Normal pension age in Norway is 67.
Haagensen said the compromise meant women would not be discriminated against on the question of retirement age.

The reports said the parties also agreed on minor pay rises for workers of at least 0.80 Norwegian crowns ($0.118) per hour on a carefully calibrated formula, depending partly on whether or not they enjoy the right to local pay talks on top of nationwide negotiations.
The talks were supplementary to the two-year central wage negotiations which took place last year.

Wage negotiations in Norway normally lead to agreement after mediation, but last year a series of strikes that hit offshore and manufacturing industries marred the country's labour scene for a few months after mediators failed to bring parties together in time.
